clue.text: Is one at Billingsgate to get such after 27?

definitions.meaning: surface reading: a question about a shopper at London's old fish market
setter's reading: a miser would buy a flatfish at a knock-down price once it has passed its sell-by date (27 across)

explanation.surface: A riddle about who would buy fish at Billingsgate once it has gone past its sell-by date.
explanation.walkthrough: Billingsgate is London's wholesale fish market; split the answer into two words and it is a cheap flatfish, the sort a penny-pincher buys when it is out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is someone who will only buy marked-down goods, so the person and the bargain fish share one name.

clue.text: Shorten intro to Catch 22

indicators.note: an intro is the opening, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of Catch
22 down is SAUCE, in the sense of cheek; lip is impudent talk too

explanation.surface: A suggestion to trim the title of Joseph Heller's novel Catch-22.
explanation.walkthrough: The 22 is not Heller's number but a cross-reference to 22 down, whose answer means insolence as well as a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: To clip something is to cut it shorter, as with hair or a hedge; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: 1D only contains rear view of actor

indicators.note: one word holding another inside it signals that one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: 'only' and 'except' both mean but, as in 'I would, only I'm busy'

indicators.note: looking only at the back of the word means taking just its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of actor

explanation.surface: A film clip showing an actor from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 1D refers to the answer of 1 down, CLIP, which here is the definition. The R goes inside EXCEPT, between the C and the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip is a short extract from a film or broadcast, which is what an excerpt is.

clue.text: After surgery lips are initially luminous — becoming yellow

indicators.note: surgery cuts and rearranges things, so the letters operated on are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it qualifies

parts.note: the first letter of are
taken as written

explanation.surface: After cosmetic surgery, someone's lips glow and then turn a jaundiced colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' reads as the colour the lips turn, but it is the slang sense of cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is slang for cowardly, and pusillanimous means lacking courage or resolve.

clue.text: Almost swim under anchor to get fishy meal

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece lying under another means it is written after it

parts.note: a kedge is a small anchor

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: when your head swims it reels

explanation.surface: Going for a swim from an anchored boat, then cooking a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A kedge is a light anchor used to haul a boat along; 'swim' is meant in the sense of a head that swims, not of swimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is a dish of smoked fish, rice and eggs, so a fishy meal describes it.

clue.text: Clobber group of workers going to French city endlessly

parts.note: TU is a trade union

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Strikers attacking a delegation of workers heading to a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like a verb meaning hit, but it is British slang for clothes or gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Clobber is British slang for clothing, and a tunic is a loose garment, so one is an example of the other.

clue.text: Some fantastic wine

indicators.note: some of a word means just a portion of its letters, sitting inside it

parts.note: the letters sit inside fantastic

explanation.surface: Praise for an excellent bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy, named after its town of origin.

clue.text: Place with vermin about is a new business

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to place something is to put it
rats are vermin

explanation.surface: A cheap rented space overrun with rodents, home to a fledgling company.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are reversed together, the whole of the place-and-vermin phrase read from the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A start-up is a newly founded company, typically small and aiming to grow.

clue.text: What one on bender at one could be later?

definitions.text: What one on bender at one could be later?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: 'could be' suggests the letters might take another form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: bender and at, then one as the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A riddle: how might someone on a drinking spree be at one o'clock in the morning?
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'one on' puts I on top of the rearranged letters. The whole clue also reads as the definition, a near &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bender is a drinking spree, and someone on one will end up drunk, which is what inebriated means.

clue.text: Peruvians once home get lots of money

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: lots of something is most of it but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: People who were once from Peru come home to a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lots of money' reads as a fortune, but it means most of the word for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca empire ruled Peru until the Spanish conquest, so its people are Peruvians of the past.

clue.text: Belittle lad with one good grade

parts.note: Den is a short form of the man's name Dennis
I is the Roman numeral for one
G is the abbreviation for good
to grade something is to rate it

explanation.surface: Putting down a boy who has scraped a single decent mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lad' stands for a man's short name, Den, a slightly loose use since nothing marks him as young.
explanation.definitionFit: To denigrate is to disparage or run someone down, which is to belittle them.

clue.text: A gunboat may be travelling around an American naval base

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap the short word
things that are travelling are on the move, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warship sailing around a US naval station.
explanation.walkthrough: AN sits after the first two letters of the rearranged phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Guantanamo Bay in Cuba is the site of a long-standing United States naval station and detention camp.

clue.text: Ride posh car to Ascot — travelling with royalty

parts.note: a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce

indicators.note: travelling letters are on the move, so they settle in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Being chauffeured in a Rolls-Royce to Royal Ascot races in company with the Royal Family.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is a famous horse-race meeting attended by the royals.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller coaster is a fairground ride on a steep, twisting track, so it is one example of a ride.

clue.text: Cheeses cut by daughter — and nuts cracked by one for wedding guest

indicators.note: something cut by a piece has that piece slicing into its middle

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: a shell cracked by something lets that thing get inside

parts.note: nuts means crazy
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wedding buffet: cheese being sliced by a daughter, nuts being cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like food to crack at the buffet, but it means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridesmaid attends the bride at her wedding, so she is one of the guests in the bridal party.

clue.text: Once more found wagon capsized in long grass

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass-like plant

indicators.note: a capsized vehicle is upside down, so in a word read across the letters run backwards

parts.note: a cart is a wagon

explanation.surface: A farm wagon has overturned in a meadow of tall grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed cart goes inside REED.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrace something is to go back over it and so locate it again, as in retracing one's steps.

clue.text: University chief backing brilliant work in Latin

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university
top means chief or foremost

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the following word's letters run the other way

parts.note: A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A university head supporting an excellent piece of Latin scholarship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like supporting, but it turns the A1 for brilliant round.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More wrote his book about an ideal island society in Latin in 1516.

clue.text: Game some shops kept under cover

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece kept under another is written below it, so it comes second

parts.note: a pall is a cloth covering, as over a coffin
a mall is a group of shops

explanation.surface: A sport played in a shopping centre with a roof.
explanation.walkthrough: The game, an old mallet-and-ball one, also gave its name to the London street Pall Mall.
explanation.definitionFit: Pall-mall was a seventeenth-century game of driving a ball through a hoop with a mallet.

clue.text: Old chief died leading kingdom

indicators.note: something leading goes in front, so that piece is written first

parts.note: d. is the abbreviation for died
O is the abbreviation for old
main means chief, principal

explanation.surface: A former ruler who died at the head of his realm.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a territory under one ruler's control, the same idea as a kingdom or realm.

clue.text: Mark's fury about a boss

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the short word that follows

parts.note: fury is great anger
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Mark is furious with his boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark's' looks like a name, but is just M; the A goes inside ANGER after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager runs a team or business, so is the boss of the people in it.

clue.text: Good shot behind farm building bags large kind of goose

indicators.note: behind means following, so that piece comes after the other

parts.note: a barn is a farm building

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it in a sack, so one piece holds another

parts.note: an ace is an excellent shot, as in tennis
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter behind the barn bags a big goose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good shot' suggests a hunter, but it is a winning serve in tennis; 'behind' and 'bags' both work on it.
explanation.definitionFit: The barnacle goose is a black-and-white Arctic species, once thought to hatch from shellfish.

clue.text: On top of chimney Santa broke a game

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of chimney

indicators.note: broke means smashed into pieces, so the letters of Santa are rearranged

explanation.surface: Father Christmas, perched on a chimney, smashed a toy he was delivering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Santa broke a game' reads like a toy being broken; 'broke' works only on Santa, and a sits outside as itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs, popular in the mid twentieth century.

clue.text: Rehoboam carries good book

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Rehoboam, King of Judah, was the son of King Solomon
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A large champagne bottle comes with a fine read; a rehoboam is a bottle holding six standard ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Rehoboam looks like the bottle size, but it is the biblical king; G goes after the first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Song of Solomon is a book of the Old Testament, a collection of love poems.

clue.text: Condiment well spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of means said out loud, so the word is judged by sound, not spelling

parts.note: a well is a source of water; the two words sound alike in a British accent

explanation.surface: A condiment with a good reputation, highly praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well spoken of' reads as highly regarded; it actually means a word for well, said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauce is a liquid accompaniment to food, and condiment covers sauces and seasonings.

clue.text: Left snooker club without tip

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a cue is the stick used in snooker
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone left the snooker hall without leaving a tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without tip' suggests a cue lacking its leather tip, but 'without' means outside and 'tip' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a useful hint, and a hint pointing towards a solution is a clue.

clue.text: Finally ruins ragout with an awfully bitter substance

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled
finally points to the closing letter of ruins

explanation.surface: A cook's last touch wrecks a stew by adding something horribly bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' takes S from ruins; 'awfully' shuffles S with RAGOUT and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Angostura bitters is an aromatic flavouring made from gentian and herbs, used in cocktails.

clue.text: Scoop on a boat contains small plant

indicators.note: to contain is to hold within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a bail is a scoop for throwing water out of a boat
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A bailer on a boat has a small plant inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an aromatic herb, so it is one particular plant.

clue.text: Unlit rescue vessel behind dam

indicators.note: behind means following, so that piece is written second

parts.note: in pedigrees D stands for dam, a mother animal, and S for sire
Noah's ark rescued the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: A lifeboat moored unlit behind a reservoir wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dam' looks like a barrier for water, but it is a mother animal, abbreviated as in breeding records.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere unlit has no light in it, and so is dark.

clue.text: When beastly Del might be rotten

definitions.text: When beastly Del might be rotten

indicators.note: something rotten has decayed and fallen apart, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking when a nasty man called Del might go off, like old food.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue loosely doubles as the definition: past this date, food might be rotten. Del suggests Del Boy, the wide boy of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-by date marks the point after which shop food should not be sold, as it may be going off.
